questions.stem: He was so tired that he _____ asleep immediately.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Fell asleep' (simple past of 'fall asleep') fits the past context. 'fallen' needs an auxiliary ('had fallen'); 'fall' is present tense.
B is correct. 'Neither...nor' is the standard correlative conjunction pair. 'Neither...or' is incorrect.

questions.stem: The manager was _____ with the employee's performance.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Was satisfied' (past passive adjective) fits. 'Satisfying' describes what causes satisfaction; 'satisfactory' is an adjective meaning adequate but wouldn't follow 'was' here in this context.

questions.stem: He could not _____ the temptation to eat the cake.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Resist' (bare infinitive) follows 'could not'. 'Resist to' is incorrect — resist takes a direct object without 'to'.

questions.stem: The government has _____ new policies to boost the economy.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Has implemented' (present perfect) is correct. 'Has implement' and 'has implements' are grammatically wrong; 'has implementing' needs a participle verb 'been'.

questions.stem: The team worked together to _____ the project on time.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'To complete' (infinitive) follows 'to'. 'Completing' needs a continuous marker; 'completed' needs an auxiliary; 'completion' is a noun.

questions.stem: The ruins of the ancient temple were a precious _____ of a once great civilisation.
questions.explanation: D is correct. A 'relic' is a surviving object or remains from an earlier time. 'Remnant' refers to a leftover portion; 'memory' is mental; 'sign' is too vague.

questions.stem: Not only did he refuse to help, _____ he also criticised the entire effort.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The correlative conjunction 'not only...but (also)' is the standard structure. 'And' could work loosely but 'but' is the prescribed pair for 'not only'.

questions.stem: Despite the heavy rain, the event proceeded _____ planned.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'As planned' (conjunction + adjective/participle) is correct. 'Like' is a preposition and cannot introduce a clause; 'how' and 'that' don't fit grammatically here.
